subject.title: fix(agents): hard-deadline runtime auth refresh to prevent gateway deadlock

question: Is it acceptable for runtime-auth and OAuth deadlines to release local ownership and allow retry while an abandoned provider, keychain, or token operation may still complete externally?
rationale: The patch prevents the identified local credential-state races, but whether concurrent late external provider effects are acceptable depends on provider and credential-store contracts that repository source alone cannot establish.

options.title: Accept bounded abandonment
options.body: Accept the documented semantics because local credential writes are generation- and ownership-guarded, while the availability benefit of unwedging agent lanes outweighs residual external-operation overlap.

options.title: Require stronger cancellation contract
options.body: Pause for a provider-owner design that adds cancellation, a provider-specific idempotency guarantee, or a stricter serialization boundary before releasing the lock.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded abandonment
recommendation.body: Accept the documented semantics because local credential writes are generation- and ownership-guarded, while the availability benefit of unwedging agent lanes outweighs residual external-operation overlap.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged OAuth contention and secret-egress work defines the adjacent auth and credential-safety boundaries involved in the decision.
